plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that bears fragrant, five-petaled flowers on bare branches in late winter. It is celebrated across East Asia, and ume plum festivals draw crowds in Japan and China at this time of year.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (late January to March)
plants.location: Japan, China, Korea (native); cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms traditionally herald the end of winter in East Asia and bloom weeks before cherry blossoms. In Japanese culture they symbolize perseverance because they flower in the cold.

plants.name: Galanthus nivalis
plants.description: A small bulbous perennial with nodding, bell-shaped white flowers marked with green on the inner petals. It often pushes up through snow and carpets woodlands and gardens in late winter.
plants.location: Europe, from the Pyrenees to Ukraine; naturalized in the UK and North America
plants.funFact: Snowdrops produce galantamine, a compound used in medicines for Alzheimer's disease. Enthusiasts called galanthophiles pay high prices for rare cultivars.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub with fluffy, golden, fragrant flower balls. Its blooming runs from late winter into spring, and it is a vital food source for native insects and birds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October, with early blooms in some regions)
plants.location: Southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Plumeria rubra
plants.description: A tropical deciduous shrub or small tree with thick succulent branches and clusters of waxy, intensely fragrant flowers. It thrives in warm climates and often blooms through the warmer months in the tropics.
plants.bloomingSeason: Warm season; in the tropics, flowering can occur most of the year, including February in the Southern Hemisphere summer
plants.location: Native to Central America, Mexico and the Caribbean; widely grown in Hawaii, Southeast Asia, Africa, and Australia
plants.funFact: Frangipani flowers are strongest in scent at night to attract hawk moths, yet the flowers offer no nectar and trick pollinators by mimicry.
